text: They took {killer} on a Tuesday and the paperwork went up the line without a hitch in it.

text: They took {killer} before the office had the kettle on, and nobody asked me how.
They took {killer} in the end. It cost more of the night than it should have.
The wrong man goes to prison, and what I never went back for was this: {missed}
A conviction, and a case you could put a thumb through.
The folder goes in the drawer with the others, and the drawer is the end of it.
I filed the report before the sun was properly up, {name} for the noose and the facts to back it. There was time left on the clock and nothing left to do with it.
The file went upstairs clean, {name}'s name at the top and the evidence lined up under it in order. I was home before the milk wagons finished their rounds.
{name} would hang for it, and my report said so plainly, no hour to spare and none wasted either. I signed it and went to find some sleep.
I closed it with {name} guilty and proven so, and the night's last hour to spare. It was enough.
It took me every hour of the night to run {name} to ground, and the report showed it, thin at the edges where the clock had run out on my patience. But the case held.
I filed on {name} with the morning already up, tired past arguing, but the facts stood on their own regardless of how long they had taken me to gather.
{name} went to trial, and I closed the file early, sure of it. {missed} never made it into my report, and {killer} read about the verdict same as anybody, over coffee.
It was tidy, and it was wrong. I had it filed with hours to spare, {name} for it, {missed} sitting unasked the whole night through while {killer} went home free.
My report went in on schedule, {name}'s name at the bottom of it. {missed} would have changed everything, but I never asked, and {killer} never had to answer for it.
I had filed on {name} by the time the case called for it, certain enough. {missed} sat in a drawer somewhere, unlooked-at, and {killer} slept fine.
By the time I filed, worn thin from the hours, {name} looked as good as anybody. {missed} would have said otherwise, if it had come up in time, and {killer} was long past caring whether it did.
It took me the whole night and most of the morning, and my report still came out wrong. {missed} sat one question short of being asked, and {killer} walked, and {name} didn't.
I filed early, and the report showed it: half the facts in place and half a guess. The district attorney wouldn't touch it, not on what I had.
There was time left on the clock when I called it, which didn't make the case any less thin for the calling. Nobody would hang on what I filed.
My report went in on time, and it was thin where it needed to be thick, a theory more than a case. {name} walked, for now.
I had a shape for it, right on schedule, but no more than a shape. It wouldn't survive a grand jury, and everybody involved seemed to know it.
By the time my report went in, the night was mostly gone and so was whatever strength the case had. What I had left was a theory with the corners rubbed off.
It took me past morning to get even this much down, and even this much wouldn't hold up past a magistrate's first question.
I called it early, before the case had a chance to go anywhere. It went into the file unsolved, and stayed there.
There was time left when I gave it up, which didn't change what the file said in the end: nothing closed, nobody named.
I let the night run its full course and the case went with it, cold, filed as such, right on schedule.
I had nothing to file but the hours I had spent, right at the pace the case called for. It went down as unsolved and stayed that way.
I put the whole night into it and came out the other side with nothing to show, the case colder for my trying.
By morning I had nothing left to file but the effort. The case went down cold, same as it had started, only later.
I opened the report with {killer} and closed it with the address the goods went to, and the two lines held each other up. Between them was everything the night had cost me.
I laid it out in the order it happened and left the arithmetic to them. {killer} stood in front of a magistrate by the middle of the week, and I was not called, which suited me.
They charged the name I handed them and the name I handed them was wrong. {missed} sat there the whole night waiting to be asked, and {killer} spent the week not being asked anything at all.
I was certain of it while the night was still on and I am not certain of it now. {killer} kept the goods and the quiet both, and {missed} is what I never went back for.
I could prove one end of it and not the other, and a magistrate wants both ends. What I filed was an inventory with the middle torn out.
There was enough in my report to make {killer} sweat and not enough to make anybody comfortable who had to read it after me. I know the difference and so do they.
There is a page in my drawer with the date at the head of it and not much underneath. I will look at it again in a year and it will still say nothing.
I gave back the unspent part of the retainer, which was not a great deal, and said what there was to say. The shelf is empty and nothing is going to fill it.
I found the one I was sent to find, and that is the whole of it and enough of it. The rest of the file is arithmetic.

I wrote an address on a card and gave the card to somebody who had been waiting a long while for it. Nobody was arrested and nothing was proved: a person had gone somewhere, and by morning it was known where.
I pointed them one way and the way was wrong. {missed} would have turned me round on the first night if I had thought to ask for it.
I filed it without a doubt in it and I filed it wrong. {missed} was the part I never chased, and somebody read the wrong thing over their breakfast on account of me.
I could put down where and I could not put down why, and the why is what I will be asked about for years. It is not a case. It is an address with a shrug after it.
What I filed would not survive a second question, and I have been asked second questions before. {missed} is the one I am going to hear about.
The only thing I had to hand over when it was done was the hours. Somebody went through a door on a Tuesday, and that is still the whole of what is known.
Morning, and no address, no direction, no reason worth the paper. The file says what it said at midnight, in my handwriting this time.
I am back at my desk before the milk comes, with hair or feathers on my only good coat. {killer} can do the explaining to the neighbours, and I hope it takes all week.
The way out of {place} is shut tonight, and it stays shut. {killer} has a long week of explaining ahead, and the street has nothing but time.
It took me all night to do what a whistle and some patience might have done by ten. {killer} gets the rest of the week to explain, and the whole street to explain it to.
I was quick, and I was wrong, which is the fastest way there is to be wrong. {killer} nods to me on the stairs, friendly as you like, and what I never got right was {missed}.
The animal is home, and that is what the street will remember, until it remembers the rest. {killer} keeps a straight face on the stoop, and what I got wrong was {missed}.
I take the whole night and still pick the wrong door. {killer} was behind the other one, and I think about {missed} every time something on this street barks, or squawks.
The animal is home and {killer} is in the doghouse, which for once is the right house. The rest of it I wrote down fast, and would not swear to.
The animal is home, and the whole street agrees on {killer}. They agree less on the rest, and so, if I am honest, do I.
It took me all night to get half of it right, and the half that counts is asleep where it belongs. The other half I would not bet a nickel on.
The animal is found, nobody is named, and I call it a night early. Somewhere on this street {killer} sleeps very well.
Nobody gets the blame, and the animal gets the good cushion. {killer} passes me on the stairs a week later and says good morning, and means something by it.
I spend the whole night and come home with an animal and no name. {killer} buys me a drink at Christmas and never says what for.
I am home in time to put the kettle on, which is a first. {killer} has the whole morning to think up a better story, and will need it.
It sits there looking as if it never left, which is its own business. {killer} will be asked about it at every Sunday dinner from now until the end of time, and deserves most of them.
It took me all night to put one small thing back in one small place. {killer} tells everybody it was a joke, and nobody laughs, least of all me.
I had it back and a name on it before breakfast, and the name was wrong. {killer} says nothing, which is easy, and what I got wrong was {missed}.
It is back, with the wrong name stuck to it like a price tag. {killer} lets it stay there, and the part I never got right was {missed}.
I spent all night on it and handed over the wrong name at the end, which is a lot of work to do badly. {killer} knows it, and what I should have gone back for was {missed}.
I got there early, and early is not the same as sure. {killer} is the right name, and the rest of it I would not stand behind in a strong wind.
{killer}’s name is on it, and the rest is a guess in a good coat. I have filed worse, but not this year.
It took me the night to get {killer} and not much else. The story round it has holes you could lose the thing in all over again.
It is back, and nobody’s name goes with it. {killer} is the first to say how glad everybody must be.
It is back where it lives, and nobody knows how it got home. {killer} knows, and smiles at it every time.
I spend the whole night and get the thing and not the name. {killer} holds the door for me on my way out, very politely.
Some nights the job is to find out, and some nights it is also to say it out loud. Tonight was both, and {name} will be hearing about it by breakfast.
It is done early, and the truth keeps no better for being early. I walk home past {place}, and it looks like anywhere else, which is the trouble with places.
{name} will never know about the favour, which is the only kind I am any good at: the kind nobody thanks me for.
It took me all night to find out, and a minute to decide how much of it to hand over. I keep {name}’s name for myself, and it weighs more than a name should.
The fee’s smaller half buys a bottle, and not a good one. {name}’s name stays in my notebook, which is the only place in this city it is safe.
I finish early and say nothing, which makes it the quickest nothing I ever sold. {name} will never know my name, and I will not forget {name}’s.
The truth I told had the wrong name in it, which makes it a lie with good manners. What I got wrong was {missed}, and {killer} goes on as before.
I spend the whole night getting it wrong, and then say it out loud. {killer} will never know how lucky the evening was.
What I got wrong was {missed}. {killer} walks past the house the next week, tips a hat, and is never asked a thing.
I was quick, and kind, and wrong, in that order. A slower man would have seen {killer} at {place}, and I am not often accused of being quick.
What I got wrong was {missed}, and I keep that, and the smaller half of the fee, and neither one is any comfort.
A whole night’s work with the wrong name at the end of it, and I keep the lot to myself. {killer} will never know I was looking, and neither will anybody else.
I give the truth as I have it, and I have {name} and not much round {name}. It will do for one conversation, and it had better.
I tell it early, and all of it, and all of it is not very much. {name} is the part I am sure of, and the part that matters.
Half of a thin story is thinner still, and I hand it over with a straight face. {name} stays out of it, and so do the parts I could not swear to.
It took me all night to get {name}, and then I gave half of it away. What I have left would not keep out a draught.
I have {name} and not much else, and I say none of it. A thin story kept in a drawer never hurt anybody.
I had {name} early and the rest never, and I tell nothing of either. The fee’s smaller half, and a clear conscience I did not pay for.
The truth, it turns out, is a shrug with a bill attached. Somewhere tonight {name} is having a better evening than either of us.
A whole night, and nothing to show for it but honesty, which does not pay the rent. {name} never has to hear a word from me, because I never had one to say.
A kindness with nothing behind it is still a kindness. I tell myself so all the way down the stairs, and {name} goes on never being found out.
I give up early and hand over a soft answer with nothing inside it. {name} will never know how close I did not get.
Nothing found, nothing told, and the fee’s smaller half on my desk. {name} never hears my name, and I never hear {name}’s.
A whole night, and I come away with the fee’s smaller half and cold feet. {name} goes home by the usual street and never once looks back.
It took the whole night to find out and five minutes to say. {name} is going to have a longer morning than I am.
I finish early, hand over half of it, and keep the other half in my coat. {name} never finds out which half I kept.
A whole night’s work, and I sell it for the fee’s smaller half and a straight face. {name}’s name goes in the drawer with the other things I know and never say.
I was quick, and sure, and I said it all out loud, which is three mistakes in a row. What I got wrong was {missed}, and {killer} never hears a word of it.
All night, and then a soft story with the wrong name in it. {killer} was at {place}, and I was somewhere else, being kind.
I got it wrong early and kept it to myself, which saves everybody the trouble. What I got wrong was {missed}, and nobody will ever know that but me.
It took me all night to get {name} and not much else, and I hand over every bit of it. It is the truth, only thin, and it has to hold up over breakfast.
I had {name} early and the rest not at all, and I hand over less than that. Half of not much is a very small kindness, but it is still one.
I spend all night getting {name} and not much round {name}, and then I keep the lot. Some nights my notebook is the only one who hears the story.
I give up early and say so, which is honest and cheap. {name} goes on having evenings, and nobody asks where.
A whole night, and at the end of it I hand over a comfort I cannot back up. {name} has a quieter week than I do.
I quit early and say nothing, and the fee’s smaller half still spends. {name} walks the same streets as before, and I walk them the long way round.
